overall_intent: A concentrated athlete holds a recurve bow at full draw in a short-distance outdoor practice lane; improve the readable relationship between hands, bow, arrow and string while preserving the supplied face-and-hair reference.

contact_point.reason: The held draw depends on separate but connected hand, grip, string and arrow-nock contacts.
contact_point.expressive_goal: Let the viewer read one real loaded bow mechanism through the athlete's purposeful contacts.
observable_targets: left palm bearing on the central bow grip
drawing fingertips hooked around the taut string at the arrow nock
both string segments connected between bow tips and nock
owner_relations: one athlete owns both working hands
one arrow nock joins the same string held by the right fingers
both feet support that athlete on the grass
required_constraints: use the supplied face-and-hair appearance reference
preserved_choices: working equipment and both feet inspectable in one original image
open_scope: camera obliquity and framing for readable endpoints
contact_point.role_focus: Readable recurve archery contact at full draw: athlete left palm bearing on bow grip, right fingers hooking taut string below jaw, arrow nock on that same string, both recurve bow tips and string segments visibly connected.
contact_point.scene_context: One woman athlete with the supplied face-and-hair reference stands on grass in an outdoor practice lane, aiming toward a straw target. Quiet afternoon light and full-body framing.

grounds.quote: The extended bow arm and anchored drawing hand visibly transmit a single loaded string through the arrow nock.

review.author: Codex
review.rationale: This role develops the independently frozen connected-load priority; it requests visible contact refinement without inferring age, identity, winning or biography.
